summary: Milestone 2026.04.99 closed in a 10 minute operational slice with 2 completed items, averaging 5 minutes each. The only material slow item was the arXiv Bundle v10 closeout, which consumed the full 10 minutes because it was serialized behind Exp 1269 critical paper fixes and then had to compile and package the TeX bundle. GPUs were idle with no GPU processes, so there was no zombie-process waste, but the milestone still left parallel GPU capacity unused for independent GPU-eligible work.

zombie_process_assessment.note: There were no material zombie processes wasting GPU resources under gpu_monitor.py's >=1024 MB and idle-time criteria.

improvements_suggested: Pre-warm TeX dependencies and cache successful compile artifacts before the gated arXiv bundle step.
Split milestones into explicit CPU-doc, CPU-artifact, and GPU-inference lanes so idle GPUs are filled whenever independent GPU work exists.
Make DualGPURunner the default for paired SOTA GGUF experiments: Qwen on GPU 0 and Gemma on GPU 1.
Add structured per-stage timing fields to conductor artifacts: gate_check_s, preflight_s, implementation_s, compile_s, packaging_s, docs_s, and upload_s.
Emit terminal blocked or gated artifacts for manual or external actions such as arXiv upload pending, so closeout does not depend on prose-only status.
Batch changelog, roadmap, status, and result reconciliation at phase boundaries instead of after every small operational step.
Run gpu_monitor.py before launch and at closeout, and only kill processes above the existing zombie threshold to avoid treating 4 MB driver residuals as material leaks.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add conductor per-stage timing and gate-open timestamps so future retros can identify whether gating, compile, tests, or docs consumed the wall time.
Pre-warm and cache TeX/arXiv bundle dependencies before paper-fix gates open, leaving only final compile and package on the critical path.
Schedule independent GPU-eligible tasks through DualGPURunner by default while publication and docs tasks run on CPU lanes.
estimated_time_savings_rationale: A 30% saving is realistic for the next similar closeout: pre-warming TeX and gate checks can remove part of the 10 minute publication critical path, parallel CPU/GPU lanes can use otherwise idle hardware, and batched reconciliation can keep docs out of the critical path.
